big_idea: We can model ANY town situation. Pick a topic from your life, ask a question, build a model.
learning_intention: We are learning to model a real-life town situation from our own life.
student_learning_goal: I can model a real-life town situation from my own life.
success_criteria: I can pick a town situation that interests me.
I can walk through the modelling cycle: situation, question, data, predict, reflect.
I can share my model with the class.
lesson_specific_materials: Mayor Mira and Town Tom together
Lesson 5 capstone tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Now you model YOUR town. Pick a situation. Walk through all 5 steps. Mira opens: 'Math lives in our town —' Class: 'and WE are the math!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Mayor Mira + Town Tom together. 'Friends — today you become MATHEMATICAL MODELLERS. Pick a town situation. Walk through the cycle: SITUATION, QUESTION, DATA, PREDICT, REFLECT.'

Show the modelling cycle chart. 'You've practiced each step. Today you do them ALL together.'

Show examples:
- 'My local park: how many slides? How many kids use them on Saturday?'
- 'My library: how many books per day? How many in a week?'
- 'My corner store: how many candies sold each lunch? In 5 days?'
- 'My bus stop: how many buses per hour? In 5 hours?'

'Pick something from YOUR town life. Walk through the 5 steps. We share at the end.'

Show the capstone template. 'Five sections: SITUATION, QUESTION, DATA, PREDICT, REFLECT. Fill them in for YOUR town topic.'
student_actions: Look at the modelling cycle chart.

steps.instruction: Hand out capstone templates. Children pick a topic and walk through the modelling cycle.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Use the template. Walk through ALL 5 steps.'

steps.instruction: Children work for 12-15 minutes individually. Teacher circulates and prompts.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Check completeness.

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge: include a refinement based on imagined or real data.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to extending children: 'Add a refinement step.'

steps.instruction: Gallery walk: children swap templates and read each other's models.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Swap with a partner. Read their model. Tell them ONE thing you liked.'

steps.instruction: Whole-class share: 5-6 children share their model aloud.
steps.teacher_prompt: Pick variety: park, library, store, bus, school.

differentiation.for_extending: Stretch: invent a model with two refinements.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide picture-supported templates with sentence frames.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Allow them to act out their model with classmates. NO-PAPER VERSION: children fold a single sheet into 5 sections labelled SITUATION / QUESTION / DATA / PREDICT / REFLECT, OR turn it into an oral capstone where each child names one cell in turn and the teacher records on chart paper.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: picks a coherent topic; walks through all 5 steps; shares with the class.
formative_check.how_to_record: Tick the capstone tracker per child.

consolidation.activity_name: Mayor Mira's Closing Brag and Certificate Ceremony
discussion_prompts: What's the most surprising model you saw today?
Why do we use the modelling CYCLE (with arrows back)?
What's something in your town you'll model after this unit?
What's the difference between data and prediction?
consolidation.exit_routine: Closing capstone refrain — Mira: 'Math lives in our town —' Class: 'and WE are the math!' Each child reads their 5-step modelling artefact aloud and points to the DATA cell their PREDICT cites.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Full modelling cycle from a child-chosen town topic.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures the C4 summative integration. Children at L4 walk through all 5 steps with a coherent town topic.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When PREDICT and DATA are disconnected — the data-as-decoration trap
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the modelling capstone, the dominant Grade-2 trap is the data-as-decoration phenomenon (Lehrer & Schauble 2002, 'Investigating Real Data in the Classroom'): children record numbers because the worksheet asks for them, but write a prediction that has no causal link to those numbers. The fix is explicit data-to-prediction grounding.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: ASK math questions (L1), COLLECT data (L2), PREDICT from data (L3), REFLECT/REFINE (L4) into a single town-modelling artefact.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair has filled in SITUATION + QUESTION + DATA but the PREDICT field reads 'we will go to recess' — disconnected from the data they collected (15 children present).
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Your DATA says 15 children. Your PREDICT says "we will go to recess." The math says: where in the prediction does the NUMBER 15 show up?'

Force the data link. 'Your prediction must USE the data. Like: "15 children today → tomorrow we predict 15 again." Or: "15 children → 75 over 5 days."'

Long-term recovery: every PREDICT field must cite at least one DATA cell.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) Cites data but doesn't extend it.
(Strong) Cites + extends data ('15 today → 15 tomorrow → 75 over 5').
(Stretched) Predicts AND names what could refine the model.
common_misconceptions: Data-as-decoration: numbers recorded but not used. (Repair: every PREDICT cites a DATA cell.)
Prediction-as-guess: PREDICT field reads as feeling. (Repair: drill 'because the data says'.)
Skipped REFINE: child stops after PREDICT. (Repair: 'what could change tomorrow's prediction?')
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — PREDICT disconnected: highlight one DATA cell, child must use that number IN the prediction sentence.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child cites data but doesn't extend: model the rate language ('15 today → 15 tomorrow because TODAY is the PATTERN').
DIAGNOSTIC C — child predicts but skips REFINE: prompt 'what could change tomorrow's prediction?' before they hand in.
